guide.title: EUR, Rome: the E42 palazzi, the lake park and the 1960 Olympic venues
guide.intro: EUR is the thirty-second of Rome's quartieri, Q. XXXII, and its official name is Europa. It was laid out from 1937 for a world exposition, the Esposizione Universale di Roma, that was to have opened in 1942 and never did. The acronym stuck. What a visitor finds today is a planned district of travertine palazzi set on wide axes, four of them designed around a single square; an artificial lake with a terraced water garden above it; a state museum with published hours and prices, a national archive with a free exhibition inside its document stores, and a planetarium; two venues built for the 1960 Olympic Games; a funfair opened in 1953; and a domed basilica at the head of a monumental stair. It is also a working business district, and it is large.

sections.heading: The exposition that never opened
sections.body:
EUR exists because of an exposition that did not take place. Law n. 2174 of 26 December 1936 created the Ente autonomo E42 to stage the Esposizione Universale di Roma in 1942, with senator Vittorio Cini as Commissario Generale. The parish of Santi Pietro e Paolo records that about 400 hectares of land belonging to the Trappist monks of the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane were expropriated to build it. Work began in 1937, slowed in the war and stopped in 1943 with much of the site unfinished, and the exposition never opened.

The buildings were completed in the 1950s, several of them for the agricultural exposition of 1953, and the quartiere took its present shape around the 1960 Olympic Games, for which the Palazzo dello Sport and the Piscina delle Rose were built. The parks were designed from 1937 and carried out after the war under Raffaele De Vico, whose name recurs on the lake gardens, the Giardino delle Cascate and the Giardino degli Ulivi. The administrative act came later still: Quartiere XXXII - E.U.R. was created by delibera n. 2453 of 13 September 1961, and renamed Quartiere XXXII - Europa by delibera n. 2509 of 5 May 1965, on the favourable opinion of the Commissione Consultiva di Toponomastica of 8 April 1965. Roma Capitale's toponymic code for the quartiere is 232.

The delibere describe the edges: the Magliana viaduct and viale di Val Fiorita, then via delle Tre Fontane and via Laurentina, to the north and east; viale dell'Umanesimo and viale dell'Oceano Pacifico to the south; and the Tiber to the west. Via Cristoforo Colombo, the former via Imperiale, runs the length of the quartiere and far beyond it in both directions, and belongs to no single zone; the Magliana viaduct is itself the northern line. The Abbazia delle Tre Fontane, whose monks planted the eucalyptus wood that is now the Parco degli Eucalipti, stands east of via Laurentina and outside this quartiere. The name Tre Fontane survives here in a street, in a funfair's address and in a park's history, and in nothing more.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
EUR is a quartiere rather than a rione, which means it is large enough that the name alone locates nothing. Steer by addresses.

Two institutions publish their own directions. The Archivio Centrale dello Stato, at Piazzale degli Archivi 27, gives Metro B to EUR Fermi, or bus 714 to Colombo/Marconi. The Museo storico della comunicazione gives its visitor entrance as Viale Europa at the corner of Via Cristoforo Colombo, by the Metro B station EUR Palasport.

The rest of the quartiere is addressed off a handful of names that recur below. Piazza Guglielmo Marconi carries the two palazzi of the Museo delle Civilta, at nos. 14 and 8, with Arturo Dazzi's obelisk at the centre of its elliptical lawn. Piazzale Konrad Adenauer carries the Palazzo degli Uffici, the Salone delle Fontane and the caffe Palombini at no. 12. Piazza Giovanni Agnelli 10 is one address for two things, the planetarium and the closed Museo della Civilta Romana. The Palazzo dei Congressi is at Piazza John Kennedy 10, La Nuvola at Viale Asia 40, the basilica at Piazzale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo 8, and the water tower with its restaurant at Piazza Pakistan. The Palazzo della Civilta Italiana stands in the Quadrato della Concordia, which is the address Roma Capitale's tourism service gives for it.

sections.heading: Opening hours, tickets and what is closed
sections.body:
Five places here publish hours a traveller can act on. The Museo delle Civilta opens Tuesday to Sunday 8.00 to 19.00, last entry 18.30, closed Monday; admission is 10,00 euro full, 2,00 euro reduced and 5,00 euro on its Amico ticket, with free entry on the first Sunday of every month and on Saturday 25 April. Its Sala Grotta Guattari is temporarily closed for maintenance. The Planetario di Roma opens Tuesday to Sunday 9.30 to 21.30, with shows at 18.00, 19.00 and 21.30, last entry an hour before closing, 10.00 to 14.00 on 24 and 31 December, and closed on Mondays, 1 January, 1 May and 25 December; its ticket office and bookshop keep winter hours of 9.30 to 18.00, and Roma Capitale's call centre is 060608, daily 9.00 to 19.00. Lo scrigno della memoria, inside the Archivio Centrale dello Stato, is free, and opens Wednesday and Thursday 10.00 to 12.00 and 15.30 to 17.00; guided visits are by compulsory booking, on Thursdays, in groups of no more than thirty, and last an hour. The basilica of Santi Pietro e Paolo opens 7.00 to 12.00 and 16.00 to 19.00, with the parish office Monday to Saturday 10.00 to 12.00. The rooftop Ristorante Il Fungo is closed Sunday and Monday and serves dinner 19.30 to 23.00 from Tuesday to Saturday.

Three things are shut, and each is shut on its own operator's word. The Museo della Civilta Romana at Piazza Giovanni Agnelli 10 is closed for refurbishment and safety works, with no reopening date stated; the planetarium in the same building is open. The Museo storico della comunicazione on Viale Europa is temporarily closed. The Torri Ligini have stood disused since the late 1990s and are under refurbishment.

No source publishes hours for several of the rest: the Palazzo della Civilta Italiana, which is Fendi's headquarters and states nothing about visitor access; the Palazzo degli Uffici; Luneur Park; the Piscina delle Rose; and the sanctuary on via Laurentina. The Palazzo dei Congressi and La Nuvola are working congress buildings whose owner publishes an events calendar rather than opening times.

faq.question: What does EUR stand for, and why is the quartiere also called Europa?
faq.answer: EUR is the acronym of Esposizione Universale di Roma, the world exposition that was to open in Rome in 1942 and never did. The unit was created as Quartiere XXXII - E.U.R. by delibera n. 2453 of 13 September 1961, and renamed Quartiere XXXII - Europa by delibera n. 2509 of 5 May 1965 on the favourable opinion of the Commissione Consultiva di Toponomastica of 8 April 1965. Both names are in use; Roma Capitale's toponymic code is 232.

faq.question: What can you actually go inside?
faq.answer: The Museo delle Civilta, in two palazzi on Piazza Guglielmo Marconi, is a full museum visit, open Tuesday to Sunday 8.00 to 19.00. The Planetario di Roma runs shows at 18.00, 19.00 and 21.30, Tuesday to Sunday. Lo scrigno della memoria, the free permanent exhibition laid out inside the Archivio Centrale dello Stato's document stores, opens Wednesday and Thursday mornings and afternoons, with guided visits on Thursdays by compulsory booking. The basilica of Santi Pietro e Paolo opens twice a day, and the parks and the lake cost nothing. The rest of EUR, the E42 palazzi included, is looked at from the outside.

faq.question: Can you go into the Palazzo della Civilta Italiana?
faq.answer: The building has housed the headquarters of Fendi since 2015, and its owner, EUR S.p.A., publishes no visiting arrangements for it; no source states its opening hours, so none are given here. What is visible from the ground is the point of it anyway: a travertine-clad block 51 metres per side and 68 metres high, eight floors of which six answer the six orders of arches, 28 marble statues of 3.40 metres under the entrance arcades, four groups of the Dioscuri by Publio Morbiducci and Alberto Felci beside the staircases, and the inscription across the frontone, Un popolo di poeti di artisti di eroi di santi di pensatori di scienziati di navigatori di trasmigratori.

faq.question: Is the Museo della Civilta Romana open?
faq.answer: No. Roma Capitale's own museum site states that it is closed for refurbishment and safety works, and no source states a reopening date. It closed on 31 January 2014, and its collections, including the complete cast series of Trajan's Column and Italo Gismondi's 1:250 model of imperial Rome, cannot currently be seen. The Planetario di Roma occupies the same building at Piazza Giovanni Agnelli 10 and is open.

faq.question: Where do you eat in EUR?
faq.answer: Thinly. EUR is an office district whose bars and restaurants are ordinary neighbourhood trade with no published history. Two have a sourced history behind them: the Ristorante Il Fungo, at the top of the 53-metre water tower on Piazza Pakistan, which serves dinner from Tuesday to Saturday, 19.30 to 23.00, and is closed Sunday and Monday; and the caffe Palombini at Piazzale Konrad Adenauer 12, which EUR S.p.A. records as still occupying the Palazzo ex Ristorante Ufficiale, a building designed by Ettore Rossi in 1939. The Hilton Rome EUR La Lama on Viale Europa occupies the 55-metre slab tower connected to the congress centre.

faq.question: Is the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane in EUR?
faq.answer: No. The abbey stands east of via Laurentina, outside this quartiere, although its monks planted the eucalyptus wood that became the Parco degli Eucalipti and about 400 hectares of their land was expropriated to build E42. What is in EUR, on via Laurentina, is a separate place: the Santuario della Vergine della Rivelazione - Madre della Chiesa, which is not part of the abbey's complex. It stands at the grotto where, on 12 April 1947, Bruno Cornacchiola said the Madonna appeared to him and his three children. The Catholic Church has not recognised the apparitions.

places.name: Palazzo della Civilta Italiana
places.summary: The travertine-clad block of six orders of arches that has become the sign of the whole quartiere, also called the Palazzo della Civilta del Lavoro. It stands on a stylobate at the end of the first decumanus, at 107 m above sea level, and measures 51 m per side and 68 m high, with eight floors, six of them corresponding to the six orders of arches. Its owner publishes no visiting arrangements, and no source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Designed by Giovanni Guerrini, Ernesto Bruno Lapadula and Mario Romano. Construction began in December 1938, stopped in 1943 and was finished after the war. It was designed for load-bearing masonry and built in reinforced concrete, clad in travertine, with two opposed monumental staircases. Twenty-eight marble statues, each 3.40 m high, stand under the entrance-level arcades, and four sculptural groups of the Dioscuri by Publio Morbiducci and Alberto Felci flank the staircases. The inscription across the frontone reads: Un popolo di poeti di artisti di eroi di santi di pensatori di scienziati di navigatori di trasmigratori. Since 2015 the building has housed the headquarters of Fendi.

places.name: Museo delle Civilta
places.summary: A state museum with two seats facing each other on the same square: the Palazzo delle Scienze at Piazza Guglielmo Marconi 14, holding prehistory, palaeontology, litho-mineralogy, the African, American, Asian and Oceanian collections, the early medieval collections, collections of colonial provenance and contemporary work; and the Palazzo delle Arti e Tradizioni Popolari at Piazza Guglielmo Marconi 8, holding Italian popular arts and traditions. It opens Tuesday to Sunday 8.00 to 19.00, last entry 18.30, and is closed on Monday. Admission is 10,00 euro full, 2,00 euro reduced and 5,00 euro on the Amico ticket, with free entry for EU citizens under 18 and other entitled categories, on the first Sunday of every month and on Saturday 25 April. The Sala Grotta Guattari is temporarily closed for extraordinary maintenance.
places.history: The museum was founded in 2016 as an institute with special autonomy of the Ministero della Cultura, and extends over about 50,000 m2 of galleries and stores. The Palazzo delle Scienze was built between 1938 and 1943 by Luigi Brusa, Gino Cancellotti, Eugenio Montuori and Alfredo Scalpelli, working in Marcello Piacentini's team; the Palazzo delle Arti e Tradizioni Popolari was designed in 1938 and built by 1942 by Massimo Castellazzi, Pietro Morresi and Annibale Vitellozzi, as a mirror image of the first around a colonnaded courtyard. The museum names the works a visitor can look for: in the atrium of the Palazzo delle Scienze, two murals by Valerio Fraschetti, La scuola di Galileo and Le applicazioni tecniche della scienza, the second left as preparatory ground when the war stopped work; above the monumental staircase the polychrome window by Giulio Rosso of 1941 to 1942; in the Salone delle Scienze the marble intarsia floor by Mario Tozzi of 1943; and in the other palazzo the marble relief Elementi caratteristici del folklore by Amerigo Tot. Two exterior mosaics of 1942 face each other across the flank of the square, Fortunato Depero's Le professioni e le arti and Enrico Prampolini's Le Corporazioni.

places.name: Palazzo dei Ricevimenti e dei Congressi
places.summary: Adalberto Libera's congress building, a base 75 by 135 m in plan and 15 m high, with the Salone della Cultura inside it as a cube of 45 m per side and the Auditorium Capitalis seating 792. It is a working congress centre, and its owner publishes an events calendar rather than visiting hours, so no general opening hours are given here.
places.history: Libera won the competition for it; Terragni, Cattaneo and Lingeri came second. Work began in 1938 and the building was completed in 1954. It held the fencing events of the 1960 Olympic Games.

places.name: Palazzo degli Uffici
places.summary: Gaetano Minnucci's building for the exposition authority, today the head office of EUR S.p.A. Work began at the end of 1937 and finished at the end of 1939. Public access is not stated by its owner.
places.history: Publio Morbiducci's travertine bas-relief La storia di Roma attraverso le opere edilizie stands over the principal entrance, and Giorgio Quaroni's La fondazione di Roma, painted between September 1939 and January 1940, is in the Sala Quaroni on the first floor. On the second basement level Minnucci built an air-raid shelter: a reinforced-concrete volume of about 475 m2, isolated from the rest of the building by a cavity of 125 cm, with metal gas-proof doors and a twin dynamo driven by two tandem bicycles to run its ventilation and lighting.

places.name: Salone delle Fontane
places.summary: A hall occupying a significant part of the Palazzo degli Uffici, built to house the ticket offices of the 1942 exposition and now used as an events and conference space. Outside it stand a monumental pillared portico and a large illuminated fountain divided into three basins, lined with opaline-green Venetian mosaic.
places.history: The fountain's perimeter mosaics, by Gino Severini, Giulio Rosso and Giovanni Guerrini, have been restored.

places.name: Palazzo ex Ristorante Ufficiale dell'Ente EUR
places.summary: The building designed in 1939 by Ettore Rossi to receive foreign delegations at the exposition: a rectangular block of three floors, porticoed on all four sides and faced in fluted gilt calacatta marble. It still contains the caffe Palombini.
places.history: Abandoned after the war, it reopened for the agricultural exposition of 1953 and was heavily altered in the 1960s, when new floors and a curtain wall replaced the original travertine facades. Two decorative works survive on the ground floor, inside what is today a commercial premises: a tempera mural by Franco Gentilini and a polychrome marble intarsia by Eugenio Fegarotti. The building housed Roma Capitale's urban-planning department until 2022, and under an agreement between EUR S.p.A. and Bulgari Gioielli it is to be regenerated as a centre for high-end craft production.

places.name: Obelisco di Marconi
places.summary: Arturo Dazzi's obelisk to Guglielmo Marconi, standing at the centre of the elliptical lawn in the middle of the square, on the axis of via Cristoforo Colombo. It is a truncated pyramid of reinforced concrete faced with 92 slabs of Carrara marble carrying high reliefs in four rows, and is given a height of 45 m.
places.history: The Ministero della Cultura Popolare commissioned it in 1939 for what was then piazza Imperiale. Work stopped in 1940 with two registers cut, resumed in 1951, and the obelisk was inaugurated on 12 December 1959.

places.name: Piazza Guglielmo Marconi
places.summary: The square that was designed as one of the fulcra of the 1942 exposition, and a useful address to steer by: the two palazzi of the Museo delle Civilta stand at nos. 14 and 8, and Dazzi's obelisk stands on the lawn at its centre.
places.history: It was originally piazza Imperiale. The palazzi around it were planned to hold four exhibitions, of science, popular traditions, ancient art and modern art, with a cinema-theatre closing the fourth side that was never built.

places.name: Archivio Centrale dello Stato
places.summary: The national archive of the Italian state, in a building of its own at Piazzale degli Archivi 27, telephone +39 06 545481. The institute gives its own directions as Metro B to EUR Fermi, or bus 714 to Colombo/Marconi. It holds the free permanent exhibition Lo scrigno della memoria.
places.history: Mario De Renzi and the studio Figini e Pollini were declared joint winners of the second competition in June 1938. The building was intended first as the Palazzo delle Forze Armate and then for an exhibition on autarky and corporatism; its foundations were begun in September 1939, and the foundations and the frame were all that stood before the war. It was completed in the 1950s under Virgilio Testa, and its public rooms, the entrance, reading room, library and conference room, were redesigned in the 1990s by Giulio Savio.

places.name: Lo scrigno della memoria
places.summary: A free permanent exhibition inside the Archivio Centrale dello Stato, laid out among the archive's document stores. Admission is free, and it opens Wednesday and Thursday, 10.00 to 12.00 and 15.30 to 17.00. Guided visits are by compulsory booking, in groups of no more than thirty, on Thursdays; school visits are booked for Wednesdays. A visit lasts an hour, and may be preceded by a thirty-minute introduction in the institute's teaching room. Reserved disabled parking is available inside the institute's car park.
places.history: The exhibition opened in March 2023, arranged in five thematic areas around one of the three originals of the Constitution of the Italian Republic. It shows over 300 documents and 50 objects and artworks drawn from 160 linear kilometres of holdings. It was conceived by Andrea De Pasquale, with a scientific committee coordinated by Guido Melis.

places.name: Museo della Civilta Romana
places.summary: The museum is closed for refurbishment and safety works. No source states a reopening date. It shares its building with the Planetario di Roma, which is open.
places.history: The museum closed on 31 January 2014. Its building was designed by Pietro Aschieri, Domenico Bernardini, Cesare Pascoletti and Gino Peressutti, winners of an E42 competition, as two parallel projecting blocks with a travertine colonnade forming the backdrop to the square. The collections, which cannot currently be seen, are plaster casts, models and dioramas of Roman civilisation, and include the complete cast series of Trajan's Column and Italo Gismondi's 1:250 model of imperial Rome.

places.name: Planetario di Roma
places.summary: The planetarium and museum of astronomy, sharing its building with the Museo della Civilta Romana. The dome is 14 m across and the room seats 98. It opens Tuesday to Sunday 9.30 to 21.30, with shows at 18.00, 19.00 and 21.30 and last entry an hour before closing, and 10.00 to 14.00 on 24 and 31 December; it is closed on Mondays, 1 January, 1 May and 25 December. The ticket office and bookshop keep winter hours of 9.30 to 18.00, Tuesday to Sunday. Roma Capitale's call centre for it is 060608, daily 9.00 to 19.00.
places.history: The planetarium has been back in operation since 22 April 2022, after works on its technology. It is part of the Sistema Musei di Roma Capitale, so the MIC card applies.

places.name: Museo storico della comunicazione
places.summary: The museum is temporarily closed. Its visitor entrance is on Viale Europa at the corner of Via Cristoforo Colombo, inside the EUR seat of the Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, by the Metro B station EUR Palasport; the telephone number is 06 5444 3000 and the office contact address is Viale America 201.
places.history: The museum covers about 4,000 m2 of rooms on the history of Italian post and telecommunications. Its holdings include post boxes, the earliest shown being one from Borgo Cerreto dated 1633, a reconstructed late nineteenth-century post office, the mails of the pre-unification states, military post, and material connected with Guglielmo Marconi and Antonio Meucci.

places.name: Parco Centrale del Lago
places.summary: The park around EUR's artificial lake, 165,130 m2 in its owner's figure, with entrances on via Cristoforo Colombo, piazzale Enrico Mattei, viale America, viale Oceania and viale Umberto Tupini. The basin is about 1 km long and between 60 and 130 m wide, and the Palazzo ENI closes its south-east short end. The planting runs to oaks, poplars, magnolias, olives and maples, with laurustinus, ligustrum, pittosporum and conifers among them.
places.history: The park was inaugurated in 1962. The Passeggiata del Giappone, which its owner describes as one piece with the circuit of the lake gardens, was designed by Raffaele De Vico and planted with flowering cherries donated by the city of Tokyo; it is part of this park rather than a separate place.

places.name: Giardino delle Cascate
places.summary: The Giardino delle Cascate covers about 42,000 m2. Raffaele De Vico designed it and it was inaugurated on 29 June 1961. It is laid out in two symmetrical sections about the axis of the central cascade, with an upper part of two hairpin promenades leading to two belvederes and a lower part of two cascades and lateral channels flanked by two cypress rotundas; a glass-floored footbridge crosses the central cascade and links the banks.
places.history: The pumping plant was modernised in 2010, and on 5 May 2017 the lowest section, about 5,000 m2 directly on the lake, opened to the public. The cascades oxygenate the lake, and belong to a water system that also takes in the lifting station on viale Oceania and the water tower known as il Fungo.

places.name: Parco del Ninfeo
places.summary: A park of 82,000 m2 named after the Fontana del Ninfeo, which was built in 1940. Via Romolo Murri, lined with a double row of plane trees and a clipped ligustrum hedge, separates it from the Parco del Turismo.
places.history: The war left the site derelict. Raffaele De Vico worked on its completion and landscape recovery from 1952, finishing in 1961.

places.name: Parco del Turismo
places.summary: A park bounded by viale Romolo Murri and via delle Tre Fontane. It holds Ercole Drei's stele-fountain La vita dei campi, dated 1940, and bas-reliefs by Bellini, both originally destined for the agricultural exhibition, together with a restored building that served as an open-air library in the 1960s.
places.history: The stele and the bas-reliefs were made for the exhibition and stayed on the site; the library building has been restored.

places.name: Parco degli Eucalipti
places.summary: A park of 91,000 m2 along via Laurentina, holding about 860 trees, predominantly eucalyptus, laid out in terraces, belvederes, paths and raised walkways, with a dog-friendly area.
places.history: The wood began as eucalyptus planted in the nineteenth century by the Trappist monks of the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane, to improve the air and to make medicinal elixirs. Design of a park here began in 1938, when the site was earmarked for a Museo Coloniale, and works broke off around 1943. The present layout is by the architect Varisco, head of the Ente EUR parks office; Raffaele De Vico's post-war proposal was never carried out.

places.name: Giardino degli Ulivi
places.summary: A pair of gardens in amphitheatre form, with travertine blocks set in an exedra, olives and tall trees. Of the two gardens, the eastern one is fenced and is used for cultural events.
places.history: Both were provided for in the 1940 exposition plan and designed by Raffaele De Vico.

places.name: Basilica dei Santi Pietro e Paolo
places.address: Piazzale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo 8, 00144 Roma RM
places.summary: The domed church at the head of the monumental stair down to viale Europa, entrusted to the Frati Minori Conventuali. It is on a Greek-cross plan, with a central cube carrying a hemispherical dome 32 m in diameter, and colossal statues of Peter and Paul flanking the portico. The parish gives the address as Piazzale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo 8 and the telephone as 06 5926166; the church opens 7.00 to 12.00 and 16.00 to 19.00, and the parish office Monday to Saturday 10.00 to 12.00.
places.history: The architects were Arnaldo Foschini, Alfredo Energici, Vittorio Grassi, Nello Ena, Tullio Rossi and Costantino Vetriani. The design was approved in September 1938 and the foundation stone laid in spring 1939; work slowed in the war and stopped after a bombardment in 1943, resumed in 1953, and the church opened for worship in July 1955. It became a parish in December 1958, received a cardinalatial title on 5 February 1965, was dedicated in June 1966 and was given the title of minor basilica in 1967. Venanzo Crocetti's marble high relief Conversione di Saulo, of 1941, is on the flank, and the organ was built in 1960 by Libero Rino Pinchi and enlarged in 1990 by Carlo Soracco. The parish's own history records the founding fact of the whole quartiere: about 400 hectares of land belonging to the Trappist monks of the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane were expropriated to build E42, and the Ente autonomo E42 was created by law n. 2174 of 26 December 1936 with senator Vittorio Cini as Commissario Generale.

places.name: Santuario della Vergine della Rivelazione - Madre della Chiesa
places.summary: A Marian sanctuary on via Laurentina, until April 2025 called Santa Maria del Terzo Millennio alle Tre Fontane. It is a place in its own right and is not part of the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane's complex. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The site is the grotto where, on 12 April 1947, Bruno Cornacchiola said the Madonna appeared to him and his three children. The Catholic Church has not recognised the apparitions. In 1956 Pius XII allowed a chapel of devotion to be built there, its custody entrusted to the Frati Minori Conventuali. In 1997 John Paul II changed the sanctuary's name to Santa Maria del Terzo Millennio alle Tre Fontane, and on 12 April 2025 a decree of Pope Francis raised it to a diocesan sanctuary under the name Vergine della Rivelazione - Madre della Chiesa.

places.name: Chiesa di San Gregorio Barbarigo
places.address: Via delle Montagne Rocciose 14, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church of entirely prefabricated concrete panels, raised on a terrace on pilotis, circular in plan, with a tall iron bell tower and a forecourt cross, lit through a red central skylight and clerestory windows. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Giuseppe Vaccaro built it between 1970 and 1972 for the parish erected on 28 January 1964. The altarpiece behind the presbytery is a work of 15 by 5 m by Piero Casentini, made in 2007 and 2008; the organ is by Fratelli Ruffatti, 1998, with 14 stops and fully mechanical action. There is a crypt below.

places.name: Palazzo dello Sport (PalaEur)
places.summary: The circular arena built for the 1960 Olympic Games, with a shallow dome and exposed reinforced concrete, its parterre a circle 46 m across. It is in use as a concert and events arena.
places.history: Marcello Piacentini designed it in 1956, with structural consultancy from Pier Luigi Nervi, and it was built between 1958 and 1960 by Ingg. Nervi e Bartoli for the XVII Olympic Games, holding the basketball and boxing events. It was modernised between 1999 and 2003, carried the name PalaLottomatica until 2018, and refurbishment works began in 2025.

places.name: Torre piezometrica dell'EUR (il Fungo)
places.summary: The 53-metre water tower on Piazza Pakistan, known as il Fungo, the mushroom. It is a working piezometric tower: it supplies the quartiere's non-potable water, feeds the cascade into the artificial lake, irrigates the lawns around the basin and supplies the fire mains.
places.history: It was built in 1957 and 1958 ahead of the 1960 Games, by the architects Aldo Capozza and Sergio Martinelli with the engineers Roberto Colosimo and Sergio Varisco. The tenor Mario Del Monaco's restaurant on the fourteenth floor, designed by Lorenzo Monardo, opened in 1964, with a bar at ground level. A bombing in September 1978 damaged the ground-floor bar, and the restaurant stayed shut until 1991.

places.name: Piscina delle Rose
places.summary: An open-air swimming pool with a basin of 50 by 25 m, built for the 1960 Olympic Games. It also houses a gym and a rowing and canoe club whose activity takes place on the neighbouring lake. No source states its opening hours or prices, so none are given here.
places.history: It was designed in 1958 and completed in 1960, as a training pool and the venue for the water-polo preliminary matches, by the architect Sergio Buonamico with the engineers Guido Gigli and Giorgio Biuso. It was refurbished in 2007, when an indoor pool and a restaurant were added.

places.name: Luneur Park
places.address: Via delle Tre Fontane 100, 00144 Roma RM
places.summary: A funfair at Via delle Tre Fontane 100, since its 2016 reopening aimed at children up to 12 and their families. No source publishes its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: It was built in 1953 as a temporary attraction inside the agricultural exposition and kept open by demand, and from 1960, the Olympic year, it opened year round. The name LunEur was adopted five years later by a referendum among the operators. At its height it had 130 family-run attractions. After nearly a decade of restoration it reopened on 27 October 2016 as Luneur Park.

places.name: Obelisco Novecento
places.address: Piazzale Pier Luigi Nervi, 00144 Roma RM
places.summary: Arnaldo Pomodoro's bronze obelisk, 21 m long and 7 m wide, standing at the centre of a circular basin at the fork of via Cristoforo Colombo.
places.history: Pomodoro executed it between 2000 and 2002 on a commission for the Jubilee of 2000, and it was inaugurated on 23 October 2004.

places.name: Ristorante Il Fungo
places.summary: A restaurant at the top of the water tower on Piazza Pakistan, with a bistro and a bar at its foot. The telephone number is 06 5921980.
places.history: The rooftop restaurant is closed Sunday and Monday. Tuesday to Saturday it serves no lunch; dinner is 19.30 to 23.00. The bistro opens Monday to Thursday 8.00 to 21.00 and Friday and Saturday 8.00 to 24.00, and is closed Sunday. The bar opens daily from 8.00.

places.name: Palombini
places.summary: A cafe at Piazzale Konrad Adenauer 12, inside the Palazzo ex Ristorante Ufficiale dell'Ente EUR. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: EUR S.p.A.'s page on the Palazzo ex Ristorante Ufficiale, the block Ettore Rossi designed in 1939, records that the building still houses the caffe Palombini.

places.name: Hilton Rome EUR La Lama
places.summary: A four-star hotel occupying la lama, the blade-shaped tower of the convention complex, which EUR S.p.A. describes as 55 m high, 15 m wide and 126 m long and directly connected to the congress centre's spaces.
places.history: No source states a history of the hotel.

places.name: La Nuvola (Roma Convention Center)
places.summary: Massimiliano Fuksas's convention centre, in three parts: la teca, a glass case 40 m high, 70 m wide and 175 m long, built with 18,000 tonnes of steel, 42,000 glass panels, 25,000 m2 of travertine and 28 lifts; la nuvola, a curved steel skeleton clad in perforated siliconed glass fibre holding an auditorium of 1,748 seats; and la lama, the tower occupied by the Hilton Rome EUR La Lama. There are over 26,000 m2 of usable space. It is a working convention centre, and no source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Fuksas won an international competition held between 1998 and 2000, whose jury was chaired by Norman Foster and whose verdict was given on 16 February 2000. The foundation stone was laid on 11 December 2007 and the building was inaugurated in 2016.

places.name: Palazzo ENI
places.summary: The glass-fronted office block that closes the south-east short end of EUR's lake. It is a private headquarters and no public access is stated for it.
places.history: It was built between 1959 and 1962.

places.name: Torri Ligini
places.summary: Five buildings, three of them seventeen-storey towers of identical height, about 67 m, linked by a two-level podium. They have stood disused since the late 1990s and a refurbishment of 140 million euro is under way, so they cannot be visited.
places.history: Cesare Ligini designed them with Vittorio Cafiero, Guido Marinucci and Renato Venturi, and they were inaugurated in 1961. They held offices of the Ministero delle Finanze for about thirty years, and have been owned by Fintecna since 2020.

places.name: Edificio delle Poste, Telegrafi e Telefoni
places.summary: The E42 post and telegraph building on Viale Beethoven, designed by the Milanese studio BBPR: Gian Luigi Banfi, Lodovico Barbiano di Belgiojoso, Enrico Peressutti and Ernesto Nathan Rogers. It is still a working post office.
places.history: Construction was ratified on 27 July 1938 and the works ran from June 1939 to 24 August 1942, with interior work continuing to 10 June 1943. Rogers was forced off the project under the fascist racial laws, and with Banfi and Belgiojoso away on war service Peressutti alone saw the building through. It was occupied by German and then American troops between 1943 and 1947 as the postal and telephone centre for southern Rome, and reopened for the agricultural exposition of 1953.

entries.name: Palazzo della Civilta Italiana
entries.note: Guerrini, Lapadula and Romano's block of six orders of arches, 51 m per side and 68 m high, begun in December 1938 and Fendi's headquarters since 2015.

entries.name: Museo delle Civilta
entries.note: A state museum in two palazzi facing each other on Piazza Guglielmo Marconi, open Tuesday to Sunday 8.00 to 19.00, free on the first Sunday of every month.

entries.name: Lo scrigno della memoria
entries.note: Free, and open Wednesday and Thursday: an exhibition inside the national archive's document stores, around one of the three originals of the Constitution.

entries.name: Planetario di Roma
entries.note: A 14-metre dome with 98 seats, back in operation since 22 April 2022, with shows at 18.00, 19.00 and 21.30 from Tuesday to Sunday.

entries.name: Obelisco di Marconi
entries.note: Arturo Dazzi's 45-metre obelisk, faced with 92 slabs of Carrara marble, commissioned in 1939 and inaugurated on 12 December 1959.

entries.name: Palazzo dei Ricevimenti e dei Congressi
entries.note: Adalberto Libera's congress building, begun in 1938 and completed in 1954, which held the fencing events of the 1960 Olympic Games.

entries.name: Palazzo degli Uffici
entries.note: Gaetano Minnucci's building of 1937 to 1939, with an air-raid shelter of about 475 m2 in its second basement powered by two tandem bicycles.

entries.name: Parco Centrale del Lago
entries.note: The 165,130 m2 park around a basin about 1 km long, inaugurated in 1962, with cherries from Tokyo along the Passeggiata del Giappone.

entries.name: Giardino delle Cascate
entries.note: Raffaele De Vico's terraced water garden of about 42,000 m2, inaugurated on 29 June 1961; its lowest section opened to the public on 5 May 2017.

entries.name: Basilica dei Santi Pietro e Paolo
entries.note: A Greek-cross church with a hemispherical dome 32 m across, opened for worship in July 1955; it opens 7.00 to 12.00 and 16.00 to 19.00.

entries.name: Palazzo dello Sport (PalaEur)
entries.note: Piacentini and Nervi's domed arena of 1958 to 1960, which held the Olympic basketball and boxing, and is in use as a concert and events arena.

entries.name: Ristorante Il Fungo
entries.note: Dinner at the top of the 53-metre water tower on Piazza Pakistan, Tuesday to Saturday 19.30 to 23.00; closed Sunday and Monday.

entries.name: Palombini
entries.note: A cafe at Piazzale Konrad Adenauer 12, inside the block Ettore Rossi designed in 1939 as the exposition's official restaurant.

entries.name: Luneur Park
entries.note: A funfair built in 1953 inside the agricultural exposition, reopened on 27 October 2016 for children up to 12 and their families.

Q. XX Ardeatino, the neighbour across via Laurentina, which the delibere make EUR's eastern line.
Q. XXXIII, on the coast, and like EUR a quartiere rather than one of the twenty-two rioni.
R. XX Testaccio, the rione at the Pyramid and the Aurelian Walls, where the road out to EUR begins.
The three-day Rome itinerary in this series. EUR lies well outside the walls and none of its places are in the historic centre.
